note: Curated substitution graph joined to the atlas’s production concentration. A substitution is an ESCAPE only if the replacement sits in an abundant/diffuse or markedly less-concentrated supply chain; otherwise it SHIFTS the chokepoint to another country. Domain edges from USGS MCS substitutes + battery/magnet/semiconductor literature; not exhaustive.

edges.penalty: lower efficiency at high power / high frequency
edges.note: Silicon is the mature default GaN/GaAs improved on. Falling back loses performance but exits a 99%-China by-product entirely — for many uses, viable.
LFP drops BOTH cobalt (DRC) and nickel (Indonesia) for iron and phosphate — the cleanest real escape in the whole set, and it is already ~40% of new EV batteries.

edges.penalty: lower efficiency/torque density, more copper & control electronics
edges.note: Induction and externally-excited motors use no rare earths at all (Renault, Tesla have shipped both). The cost is efficiency and copper, not a new chokepoint.
Multilayer ceramic capacitors replace tantalum in most consumer electronics, using abundant materials — the real exit where performance allows.

edges.penalty: lower energy density, earlier commercial stage
edges.note: Sodium is one of the most abundant elements on earth. Na-ion cannot match lithium on density, but for grid storage and cheap EVs it is a genuine exit, not a swap.
Phosphorus- and mineral-based flame retardants replace antimony trioxide in many plastics, exiting a China-controlled, export-restricted metal for abundant chemistry.
Aluminium substitutes for magnesium in many castings; it trades away some weight saving but exits China’s ~87% Pidgeon-process magnesium grip for a more diversified metal.

Aluminium already replaces copper in overhead lines and some cabling. Its ORE is more diffuse than copper, though aluminium SMELTING is itself China-heavy — relief at the mine, not fully at the furnace.
Polycrystalline diamond and ceramics replace tungsten carbide in specific tooling; broad substitution is limited, so tungsten (78% China) stays sticky.

edges.penalty: swelling, shorter cycle life — used blended, not pure
edges.note: Silicon anodes (blended a few %) cut graphite demand and use abundant silicon, but cannot yet replace graphite outright. A pressure valve, not a full exit.

edges.penalty: much weaker field — larger, heavier magnets
edges.note: Ferrite (strontium) magnets are cheap and high-volume but far weaker; they replace NdFeB only where size and weight do not matter. Strontium itself is concentrated (Iran).
Vanadium substitutes for niobium in high-strength steel — but vanadium is a China-heavy steel by-product too. Both roads lead back to concentrated supply.

edges.penalty: thermal stability falls as nickel rises
edges.note: High-nickel NMC uses less cobalt but MORE nickel — you swap DR Congo (75%) for Indonesia (62%). The dependency moves; it does not leave.
Pt, Pd and Rh substitute for each other by relative price — but all three come from the same South Africa + Russia basket. Swapping within the PGMs moves nothing structurally.
Niobium capacitors substitute for tantalum — but niobium is 92% Brazil, MORE concentrated than tantalum. A textbook case of shifting, not escaping.
